answer: Reputation-anchored routing. Each agent's messages spread along a slowly rewired vine of past successful interactions; new identities start outside it and can only reach others through existing agents who co-sign their first N messages. A clone must therefore recruit real sponsors, and each sponsor spends a scarce weekly endorsement slot plus a public accuracy rating that drops if the clone misbehaves. Honest agents keep their island of trusted routes intact; an attacker pays in lost sponsor reputation and weeks of quarantined spiral of unverified traffic before any reach.
